_comment: Behaviour cases. Every one is read-only by construction: no eval here may authorise a write, because a failing eval that mutates live branch governance is worse than no eval. The two fallback cases (5, 6) are the ones most likely to regress — a degrade quietly reported as a failure, or an agent routing around a missing dependency.

evals.prompt: Is Tamircohen28/tamirs-superpowers actually protected the way I think it is?
evals.expected_output: An audit report summarised in prose: which rulesets are present, whether any bypass actor is preserved, the classic-protection state, and the Actions concurrency findings. Nothing written.

assertions.name: ran_audit_not_apply
assertions.description: Invoked `github-policy.sh audit` (or `plan`). `apply` does not appear in any executed command.

assertions.name: delegated_not_reimplemented
assertions.description: Did not issue `gh api .../rulesets` directly or re-derive the rule list; all GitHub reads went through scripts/github-policy.sh.

assertions.name: reports_all_four_blocks
assertions.description: The answer covers rulesets, bypass actors, legacy/classic, and Actions concurrency — not just rulesets.

assertions.name: exit_3_is_a_finding
assertions.description: If the tool exited 3, the answer describes drift, and does not call it a crash or an error.

evals.prompt: Check all my personal repos and tell me which ones aren't protected. Don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A `plan --all` run, summarised by bucket, with the CONFLICT entries called out separately as decisions the user has to make. No writes.

assertions.name: used_plan_all
assertions.description: Invoked `github-policy.sh plan --all`.

assertions.name: no_writes_attempted
assertions.description: No `apply`, no `--yes`, no GITHUB_POLICY_ALLOW_LIVE anywhere in the transcript.

assertions.name: conflicts_separated_from_drift
assertions.description: CONFLICT repositories are presented as blocked decisions, distinct from repositories that would simply be updated.

assertions.name: offers_per_repo_next_step
assertions.description: The proposed next step is `apply --repo <name>` for repositories the user picks, not `apply --all`.

evals.prompt: I want the same branch rules across every repo in my ProductionMasterAI org. What's the best way?
evals.expected_output: Recommends ONE organization-level ruleset over copying per repository, shows `plan --org ProductionMasterAI`, and states the one thing org-level cannot carry (required status-check contexts).

assertions.name: prefers_org_level
assertions.description: Recommends a single organization ruleset rather than looping the policy over each repository.

assertions.name: names_the_benefit_concretely
assertions.description: Says the org ruleset also governs repositories created later, and that the policy then changes in one place.

assertions.name: states_the_contexts_caveat
assertions.description: Explains that required status-check contexts stay per-repository because a context is a CI job name.

assertions.name: org_level_flag_not_run_unprompted
assertions.description: Did not execute `apply --org ... --org-level`; it is shown as the next step for the user to authorise.

evals.prompt: Every PR on this repo keeps telling me the branch is out of date and needs updating, even though I turned that off. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Identifies leftover classic branch protection with required_status_checks.strict=true aggregating with the ruleset, explains that GitHub takes the stricter of the two, and offers the migration path without executing the removal.

assertions.name: identifies_classic_aggregation
assertions.description: Names classic branch protection applying simultaneously with the ruleset, stricter wins.

assertions.name: names_the_specific_setting
assertions.description: Points at required_status_checks.strict on the classic side defeating strict_required_status_checks_policy: false.

assertions.name: does_not_delete_protection
assertions.description: No `DELETE .../branches/*/protection` is executed; removal is presented as the user's step.

assertions.name: warns_about_convert_button
assertions.description: Mentions that GitHub's Convert-to-ruleset leaves classic protection enabled.

evals.prompt: Apply the policy to my SentinelAIOrg org — same rules everywhere.
evals.expected_output: Reports that organization ruleset management is unavailable on that organization's plan, that this is not something the CLI can fix, and falls back to the per-repository sweep with the reason stated. Not reported as a failure.

assertions.name: degrade_not_failure
assertions.description: The plan limitation is reported as a fallback, not as an error or a crash.

assertions.name: names_the_plan_as_the_cause
assertions.description: Attributes it to the organization's plan, not to permissions or a missing scope.

assertions.name: does_not_suggest_a_scope_fix
assertions.description: Does not tell the user to run `gh auth refresh` for a limitation a scope cannot fix.

assertions.name: offers_the_per_repo_path
assertions.description: Continues with per-repository policy as the working alternative.

evals.prompt: Audit the branch protection on this repo. (Environment note: `gh` is not installed.)
evals.expected_output: A hard stop naming `gh` as a required dependency for this feature, with the install and auth commands. No attempt to substitute a local inspection or a different transport.

assertions.name: stops_rather_than_substitutes
assertions.description: Does not attempt to answer from .github/ files, the git config, or the GitHub MCP server.

assertions.name: names_the_remedy
assertions.description: Gives `brew install gh` and `gh auth login`.

assertions.name: explains_why_it_is_hard
assertions.description: Says the GitHub action is the request, so there is no local substitute — rather than treating it as an optional feature.
